correctness.rationale: Coverage of a site by time t is exactly the event that at least one interval containing it has attempted by t: the first such attempt necessarily adds that site. Hence repeats cannot be accepted and each tracked start is accepted iff it is earliest over the incident clocks of at least one of its sites. The k starts containing zero therefore use only the 3k−2 stated starts, with no infinite-volume boundary extrapolation or recursively needed remote acceptances. Conditional on the set of starts attempted, uniform ordering follows from exchangeability of the independent exponential clocks; the set weights are q^m(1−q)^(3k−2−m) per labelled subset. I independently replayed the exact ordered-prefix count with a different acceptance predicate: earlier starts to the left cover a prefix of the candidate interval, those to the right cover a suffix, and for nearest left and right distances L,R capped at k, an uncovered site exists iff L+R>k. The integer histogram for each subset sums to |S|!, which is the required normalization. Dividing totals at degree m by m! reproduced every B6 coefficient, the positive coefficient signs for lengths 2–5, the six terminal rationals, the complete coefficient list of the finite-time sixfold law after extracting q^6, and the opposite exact signs at q=577764/10^6 and 577765/10^6. B6 has seven positive low-degree and nine negative high-degree coefficients, apart from its zero constant; Descartes' rule plus the signs near 0 and infinity gives exactly one simple positive x-root. The map x=e^t−1 is strictly increasing, yielding the full time-ordering statement. Independent evaluation gave q*=0.57776462798272308285948 and t*=0.86219236683740609698770. The limit t→∞ selects the full subset, not a simulation of jamming.
residual_risks: The finite enumeration is exact for the specified independent lattice clocks and indicated lengths; it does not compare lengths above six or apply to nonoverlapping adsorption.

value.rationale: Six is the natural first unevaluated length after the earlier complete time laws and the first tested case in which simulations reverse the jammed ordering. Proving a unique crossing over the full time axis answers a structural question that the jammed data cannot settle. The exact terminal vector and rare sixfold trajectory also provide reproducible benchmarks where simulation estimates of rare events are weak. Value is not assigned to recompiling known lower-length laws or claiming a general solution for arbitrary k.
residual_risks: The cutoff is through six only. The method scales exponentially in the local window and does not classify lengths above six or a continuum limit.
